notes: Checked at this exact model: 1,152-zone Mini LED backlight on an IPS panel, flat rather than curved, DisplayHDR 1000, 90 W USB-C. The only 34-inch Mini LED IPS on this list, which is why it is here - it is the one way to get real local dimming without OLED's text and burn-in trade-offs. Brightness is the figure to distrust: retailer tables print 1000 cd/m2 peak while TFTCentral lists 600 cd/m2, and the two are not reconciled by anything consulted, so a deduction is recorded in _fit_penalties rather than a number being picked here. The 1000:1 contrast is the native panel ratio before the backlight dims, not what the Mini LED array achieves. KVM not mentioned either way; height adjustment confirmed present by a review but with no travel figure.

Checked at this exact model against Lenovo's own PSREF sheet for the panel, the 384-zone Mini LED backlight, the 1500R curve and the 2.5 Gb Ethernet port. Two things are weaker than the rest. Refresh is recorded as 165 Hz because PSREF gives 165 Hz with an overclock to 180 Hz and warns the 180 Hz figure is lab data that may cause display irregularities - a retailer listing it as native 180 Hz is wrong. The 140 W USB-C figure rests on two secondary sources (ComputerBase and Geeknetic); the PSREF text retrieved was truncated before the wattage, and the sheet separately shows a 15 W USB-C port, which is a different port. If the 140 W matters to you, confirm it, because at 90 W or above the work profile awards full marks either way but the number is quoted here as if verified. This is a Mini LED backlight behind a VA panel, so it earns Mini LED's panel points while carrying VA's off-axis behaviour; the deduction for that is in _fit_penalties.
